text: Joseph Matthäus Aigner (18 January 1818, Vienna – 19 February 1886, Vienna) was an Austrian portrait painter who studied under Friedrich von Amerling and Carl Rahl. He painted portraits of Franz Joseph I of Austria and his wife Elizabeth, Franz Grillparzer, Friedrich Halm, Nikolaus Lenau, and Maximilian I of Mexico. In 1847, he married actress Fanny Matras (1828–1878). During the 1848 revolutions in Vienna, Aigner served as commander of the Academic Legion and was court-martialed for high treason, receiving a death sentence. However, Alfred I, Prince of Windisch-Grätz, pardoned him. According to Ripley's Believe It or Not!, a Capuchin friar, whose name Aigner never knew, saved his life three times—when he attempted to hang himself at ages 18 and 22 and when he was sentenced to death. Aigner died by suicide with a pistol in Vienna in 1886, and the same friar presided over his funeral. This article about an Austrian painter is a stub.
